npc_blocks.title: Red Ant Guard — Medium Monstrosity (ant), Lawful Neutral — ORDINARY, not the elite
npc_blocks.stats: AC 14 (chitin and ceremonial plate) | HP 18 (4d8) | Speed 30 ft., climb 30 ft. | STR 14 (+2) DEX 12 (+1) CON 10 (+0) INT 8 (-1) WIS 12 (+1) CHA 10 (+0)
npc_blocks.defenses: Skills: Perception +5 | Senses: darkvision 60 ft., tremorsense 30 ft. | Passive Perception 15 | Languages: Ant-cant (chemical) | CR 1/2 (100 XP) | PB +2

entries.name: Overexcited
entries.text: This guard is watching everything, all at once, and has been all night. It startles at a dropped tray, at laughter, at movement in the petal panels. It notices an enormous amount and can tell almost none of it apart. While it is standing its post in a public room it makes Wisdom (Perception) checks with disadvantage — passive Perception 10, because every single thing it has flagged so far tonight has been nothing. Back-corridor patrols away from the crowd use the full 15.

entries.name: Overkill (Cleave)
entries.text: When a single attack reduces a Red Ant Guard to 0 hit points, damage in excess of its remaining hit points carries over to one other Red Ant Guard within 5 ft. of it, and can chain onward the same way while excess remains. Overkill damage never carries to or from a Royal Ant Bulwark, a Royal Ant Firecaller, or any non-ant creature. Temporary hit points (see the Firecaller's Royal Cadence) stop the chain — excess is absorbed, not passed.

entries.name: Mandible Jab
entries.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8+2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Stoke the Gaster
entries.text: The guard plants its legs and pumps its fire gland. Its abdomen swells, glows, and hisses — anyone who can see it knows exactly what is coming, and so does the guard. Until the end of its next turn the guard is Charged, and its speed is 0. If it takes 5 or more damage from a single source while Charged, the charge ruptures: the charge is lost and the guard takes 7 (2d6) fire damage — which is, from the guard's side of it, a reprieve. Round one of the two-round charged attack.

entries.name: Ember Lance (Charged only)
entries.text: The guard vents its charged gaster in a line 30 ft. long and 5 ft. wide. Each creature in the line makes a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. Flammable objects in the line that aren't worn or carried ignite — and the outward-facing palace is built of dried flower petals. The line does not spare allies, and Red Ant Guards do NOT resist fire. A lance fired into a melee cooks the guards standing in it. The royals (Bulwark, Firecaller) resist fire and walk through it. THE GUARD DOES NOT SURVIVE IT. Venting the gland burns it hollow from the inside; the guard drops to 0 hit points and dies as the lance goes out, leaving a husk that goes on burning for a minute and will light whatever it is lying against. Every red ant knows this is what the lance costs. Round two — and the last round — of the two-round charged attack.

entries.name: How it fights
entries.text: On post, two to an aperture, facing outward. In the open they fight in numbers and stand their ground rather than disengaging — they hold the line and make noise while they do it, which is what summons the royal squad. Left to themselves they jab, because Ember Lance kills them and they know it. A guard stokes its gaster under three conditions and no others: a Firecaller orders it (Volunteer), a superior is watching and it has already failed once tonight, or it is going to die anyway and can take someone with it. That makes the lance rare and dreadful rather than routine — and it means the moment a gaster starts to glow, the party is looking at an ant that has just been spent.

npc_blocks.title: Royal Ant Bulwark — Large Monstrosity (ant), Lawful Neutral — ELITE
npc_blocks.stats: AC 17 (natural armor) | HP 105 (10d10+50) | Speed 20 ft., climb 20 ft. | STR 18 (+4) DEX 8 (-1) CON 20 (+5) INT 7 (-2) WIS 12 (+1) CHA 10 (+0)
npc_blocks.defenses: Saves: STR +6, CON +7 | Skills: Athletics +6, Perception +3 | Resist: fire | Senses: darkvision 60 ft., tremorsense 30 ft. | Passive Perception 13 | Languages: Ant-cant (chemical) | CR 3 (700 XP) | PB +2

entries.name: Ponderous
entries.text: The Bulwark can't take the Dash action and has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws. It is slow on purpose — the party can outrun it, and running is frequently the correct answer.

entries.name: Royal Chitin
entries.text: Overkill (Cleave) damage never carries to or from a Bulwark. It also has advantage on saving throws against being moved, knocked prone, or grappled.

entries.name: Hold the Line
entries.text: Difficult terrain doesn't cost the Bulwark extra movement while it is moving to place itself between an intruder and a door, stair, or aperture. Bulwarks are deployed to close routes, not to chase.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The Bulwark makes two Mandible Shear attacks, or one Mandible Shear and one Pin.

entries.name: Mandible Shear
entries.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8+4) slashing damage.

entries.name: Pin
entries.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one Medium or smaller target. Hit: 9 (2d4+4) bludgeoning damage, and the target is Pinned. While Pinned its speed is 0, attack rolls against it have advantage, and it has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws. It can use its action to escape with a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. The Bulwark can have only one creature Pinned at a time, and its speed is halved while it holds a pin. The setup this exists for: a Pinned PC cannot move out of an Ember Lance and saves against it with disadvantage.

entries.name: Interpose
entries.text: When an attack hits another royal ant within 5 ft. of the Bulwark, the Bulwark can make itself the target instead, taking the damage in that ally's place. This is how the squad screens its Firecaller — the party cannot simply focus the caster down while two Bulwarks are standing over it. One reaction per round.

entries.name: How it fights
entries.text: Moves to block the exit the party wants, not toward the party. Pins the most mobile PC — Nancy is the intended target and the pin is the intended counter to her movement — and shears whatever is still in reach. Spends its reaction on Interpose to keep the Firecaller alive. Will not pursue past the door it was told to hold.

npc_blocks.title: Royal Ant Firecaller — Medium Monstrosity (ant), Lawful Neutral — ELITE, support
npc_blocks.stats: AC 15 (chitin and censer-regalia) | HP 78 (12d8+24) | Speed 30 ft., climb 30 ft. | STR 10 (+0) DEX 14 (+2) CON 14 (+2) INT 14 (+2) WIS 16 (+3) CHA 14 (+2)
npc_blocks.defenses: Saves: CON +4, WIS +5 | Skills: Perception +5, Insight +5 | Resist: fire | Senses: darkvision 60 ft., tremorsense 30 ft. | Passive Perception 15 | Languages: Ant-cant (chemical, fluent), Common | CR 3 (700 XP) | PB +2

entries.name: Pheromone Standard
entries.text: Spell save DC 13, spell attack +5. Allied ants within 30 ft. of the Firecaller can't be Frightened and have advantage on saving throws against being Charmed. Ordinary guards do not break while it is standing.

entries.name: Royal Chitin
entries.text: Overkill (Cleave) damage never carries to or from a Firecaller.

entries.name: Kindle the Host
entries.text: The Firecaller opens its censer and breathes over up to three allied ants it can see within 30 ft. Each becomes Kindled for 1 minute: its carapace runs hot enough to read by, and any creature that is not a red ant and ends its turn within 5 ft. of it takes 2 (1d4) fire damage. This damage is rolled per Kindled ant — a creature ending its turn inside a knot of three Kindled guards rolls 3d4, averaging 7–8. Kindled ends early on any ant that drops, and ends on ALL of them the instant the Firecaller dies. This is the block's main action and usually its whole first turn.

entries.name: Cinder Bolt
entries.text: Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (3d6) fire damage. What it does on the turns it has nobody left worth heating. There is no multiattack — this creature is not a nuke.

entries.name: Royal Cadence
entries.text: Up to three allied ants within 30 ft. that can smell the Firecaller each gain 5 temporary hit points. Temporary hit points from Royal Cadence stop an Overkill (Cleave) chain — excess damage is absorbed rather than passed on. This is the deliberate counter to the party mowing down Red Ant Guards, and it costs the Firecaller its bonus action every round it wants it.

entries.name: Volunteer
entries.text: The Firecaller lays a claw on one Red Ant Guard within 30 ft. and names it. That guard immediately becomes Charged (as Stoke the Gaster) without spending its own action, and its speed is not reduced; it can use Ember Lance on its own next turn. Ember Lance kills the guard that fires it, and both of them know that. An ordinary guard will not stoke its own gaster in a fight it expects to survive — this is how the lance actually reaches the table, and it is the Firecaller spending a life to do it.

entries.name: How it fights
entries.text: Stays behind the Bulwarks and holds 30 ft. Turn one is Kindle the Host on whichever three guards are closest to the party, plus Volunteer on a guard with a clean lane. Turn two heats three more and starts Royal Cadence once the party begins dropping mooks. Cinder Bolt only when there is nothing left to buff. Does not chase, does not press a losing fight, and will fall back to call the next batch — its job is to make the swarm expensive, not to win the fight itself.

npc_blocks.title: The Red Ant Queen — Huge Monstrosity (ant), Lawful Evil — CR 13, OPTIONAL, NOT A FAIR FIGHT
npc_blocks.stats: AC 18 (natural armor and coronation regalia) | HP 348 (24d12+192) | Speed 30 ft., climb 30 ft. | STR 20 (+5) DEX 12 (+1) CON 26 (+8) INT 10 (+0) WIS 16 (+3) CHA 24 (+7)
npc_blocks.defenses: Saves: DEX +6, CON +13, WIS +8, CHA +12 | Skills: Perception +8, Intimidation +12, Performance +12, Persuasion +12 | Immune: fire | Cond Immune: charmed, frightened, exhaustion, prone | Senses: darkvision 120 ft., tremorsense 60 ft. | Passive Perception 18 | Languages: Ant-cant (chemical, absolute — every red ant in the palace hears her), Common | CR 13 (10000 XP) | PB +5

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries.text: If the Queen fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead. This is the trait that tells the players what kind of fight they are in: Hypnotic Pattern, Hold Person, and Tasha's Hideous Laughter are the party's real win conditions against anything this size, and she simply declines the first three.

entries.name: Regnal Heat
entries.text: The air above the Queen bends visibly — she is identifiable from across Canopia. Any creature that starts its turn within 15 ft. of her takes 10 (3d6) fire damage. Flammable objects in that radius that aren't worn or carried ignite, and the Throne Room is dried red petal.

entries.name: A Hive Unto Herself
entries.text: An ant queen is not one creature; she is a colony wearing a crown, which is what made the Brood Coven possible in the first place. While at least one other red ant she can see is within 60 ft., the Queen regains 20 hit points at the start of each of her turns. Clear the room of her ants and the regeneration stops — which is the only honest path to hurting her, and it is a longer job than any one fight allows.

entries.name: Vainglory
entries.text: She has never once been the second most important thing in a room. The first time each round that the Queen scores a critical hit or reduces a creature to 0 hit points, she pauses to be admired: she gains 20 temporary hit points, and each creature that can see her must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or be Frightened of her until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Siege Presence
entries.text: The Queen's attacks and Crown of Embers deal double damage to objects and structures. She does not fight carefully in her own palace, and the outward-facing rooms are petal panels.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The Queen makes three attacks: three Mandible Rends, or two Mandible Rends and one Cinderspit.

entries.name: Mandible Rend
entries.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (4d8+5) slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) fire damage.

entries.name: Cinderspit
entries.text: Ranged Spell Attack: +12 to hit, range 90 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (6d6) fire damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw or catch fire, taking 7 (2d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns until it or an adjacent creature uses an action to put it out.

entries.name: Crown of Embers (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: The Queen raises her head and the crown blazes. Every creature within 30 ft. of her makes a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 55 (10d10) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. A creature that fails by 5 or more is also knocked prone and drops one held item, which lands 10 ft. away. Read the damage before you roll it. Fifty-five is more than any of these three PCs has, and the point of the action is that they hear the number.

entries.name: Command the Loyal
entries.text: One red ant the Queen can see within 60 ft. immediately uses its reaction to move up to its speed and make one attack. She never asks twice.

entries.name: The Queen Is Not Struck
entries.text: When a creature the Queen can see hits her with an attack, she can force one red ant within 10 ft. of her to take the attack's damage instead. The ant is not permitted to refuse, and ordinary guards rarely survive it. One reaction per round.

entries.name: Survey the Room (costs 1)
entries.text: The Queen looks at one creature within 60 ft. That creature must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or be Frightened of her until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Sear (costs 1)
entries.text: The Queen makes one Cinderspit attack.

entries.name: Regnal Flame (costs 2)
entries.text: A 15-ft.-radius column of red flame erupts at a point the Queen can see within 60 ft. Each creature in it makes a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The area burns until the end of her next turn; a creature that enters it or ends its turn there takes 10 (3d6) fire damage.

entries.name: Call the Brood (costs 2)
entries.text: Two Red Ant Guards arrive from an adjoining room, the guard chambers, or the Queen's own gaster, and act on her initiative. They feed A Hive Unto Herself and The Queen Is Not Struck, so this is her healing and her armour as much as it is reinforcement.

entries.name: When and where
entries.text: On initiative count 20 (losing ties), the Queen takes one lair action. She cannot use the same one two rounds running. These only work in the Throne Room and the Core.

entries.name: The Steps Fold
entries.text: The red petal stair at the room's mouth knits shut, or peels open. The Queen chooses one entrance to seal or unseal; a creature on the stair when it closes makes a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage and being pushed back into the room on a failure. Reopening a sealed way takes an action and a DC 20 Strength check.

entries.name: The Walls Take
entries.text: A 20-ft. section of petal wall ignites — often one of the Red Ant Triumph mosaics, so she is watching her own legend burn. Each creature within 5 ft. of it makes a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw or takes 17 (5d6) fire damage. The section becomes lightly obscuring smoke and keeps burning for the rest of the encounter.

entries.name: The Throne Answers
entries.text: The floor remembers that the throne rises out of it. The Queen sinks into the red petal-stone and rises again anywhere else in the room, or a spur of it erupts under one creature she can see: DC 20 Strength saving throw or be restrained by closing petals (escape DC 20) until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: All Eyes On Her
entries.text: Every painted red ant on every wall turns its head. Each creature in the room that is not a red ant makes a DC 20 Charisma saving throw or has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn, unable to do anything in that room but be an audience.

entries.name: Effect 1
entries.text: The heat shimmer above the palace is visible from anywhere in Canopia and from the promenade on the west side. Everyone in the city has grown used to navigating by it.

entries.name: Effect 2
entries.text: Fire started within the palace does not go out on its own. It has to be smothered, and it spreads along petal panels faster than it should.

entries.name: Effect 3
entries.text: Red ants within the palace cannot be Frightened while she lives, and know the direction she is in at all times.

entries.name: How it fights
entries.text: Opens with Crown of Embers if two or more enemies are within 30 ft., because it is the loudest thing she can do. Otherwise she rends whoever is closest and spends legendary actions on Survey the Room to keep the party saving against Frightened. She spends her ants freely — Call the Brood, Command the Loyal, and The Queen Is Not Struck all treat guards as consumable, and she will burn a dozen without noticing. She does not chase, she does not leave the room, and she will stop to monologue at anyone who flatters her — which is the entire opening the party has. She would rather be admired than win.  HOW SHE ACTUALLY FALLS: Not in a fight, and not by this party at this level. Killing her takes a separate plot: a coalition, poison, cutting her off from her own colony so A Hive Unto Herself stops carrying her, or the vanity that makes her stand in a burning room to be watched. Statted here so that if the party ever does corner her, the numbers exist — at level 12 with allies this is a real boss fight rather than an execution.

notes.label: How to use this sheet
notes.text: The Muster bar above the tracker is the point — nothing is pre-staged. Dial in whatever the scene calls for and roll initiative at the table. It opens on a back-corridor patrol of 2 Red Ant Guards; add more, or add royals, as the night escalates. The Red Ant Queen sits in the muster at 0 and should almost always stay there — see her own note below. Removing a creature takes the highest-numbered one off. Counts and HP persist until you hit Reset.

notes.label: Alert ladder — what to muster
notes.text: L1 NOTICED (a fight heard, Beeatrix screams, a body found): 4-6 Red Ant Guards, no royals. L2 SQUAD (enough noise, or something specifically suspicious): add 1 Firecaller + 1 to 3 Bulwarks. L3 WILDLY OUT OF HAND (fire, an open running fight in a public room, the coronation disrupted): 8-12 guards plus a second squad. L4 LOCKDOWN: everything clusters on the Red Ant Queen, which is the party's opening to escape.

notes.label: Encounter math (3 PCs at level 6)
notes.text: Thresholds: Easy 900 / Medium 1800 / Hard 2700 / Deadly 4200. Patrol pair = 200 raw, 300 adjusted — trivial, and meant to be. 6 guards = 600 raw, 1200 adjusted. Minimum squad (1 Firecaller + 1 Bulwark) = 1400 raw, 2100 adjusted, just under Hard. Standard (1 + 2) = 2100 raw, 4200 adjusted — exactly Deadly. Maximum (1 + 3) = 2800 raw, 5600 adjusted. Maximum plus 6 guards = 3400 raw, 8500 adjusted — not a fight, that is the run-to-the-kitchens signal.

notes.label: OVERKILL (cleave) — house rule
notes.text: When one attack drops a Red Ant Guard to 0, the excess damage carries to another Red Ant Guard within 5 ft., and chains on while excess remains. Red Ant Guards ONLY — never to or from a Bulwark or a Firecaller (Royal Chitin). Temporary hit points stop the chain, which is exactly what the Firecaller's Royal Cadence is for. Written for single-target attacks, melee or ranged; area spells already hit everyone, so they do not cleave.

notes.label: The charge, and what it costs
notes.text: Stoke the Gaster is a visible tell — abdomen swelling, glowing, hissing — and the guard's speed drops to 0 while it holds. 5+ damage from one source ruptures it (charge lost, 2d6 to itself). Ember Lance then does 6d6 in a 30 ft. line, DC 12 DEX for half, AND KILLS THE GUARD THAT FIRED IT. Left alone, guards will not do this; it takes a Firecaller's Volunteer, a superior watching after they already failed once, or a guard that is dying anyway.

notes.label: Fire in a petal palace
notes.text: Bulwarks and Firecallers RESIST fire. Red Ant Guards DO NOT — an Ember Lance fired into a scrum cooks the guards standing in it, and so does an Emberbloom. The outward-facing rooms are dried flower petals: loose flammables in a lance's line ignite, a spent guard leaves a husk that burns for a minute and lights whatever it is lying against. Fire is the fastest way for either side to lose control of the night.

notes.label: The scary setup
notes.text: Bulwark Pins a PC (speed 0, attacks against them have advantage, disadvantage on DEX saves) -> Firecaller Volunteers a guard -> Ember Lance down the line the PC cannot leave, saving at disadvantage. Against Nancy at 37 HP that chain is close to lethal, and her escape check should be Acrobatics +4, not Athletics -2.

notes.label: Kindled — track it on the pills
notes.text: Kindle the Host heats up to 3 allied ants for 1 minute. Anything that is not a red ant and ends its turn within 5 ft. of a Kindled ant takes 1d4 fire, ROLLED PER KINDLED ANT — a knot of three is 3d4. This is the tax on wading into the pack to cleave, and it lands almost entirely on Nancy. Kindled ends on ALL of them the moment the Firecaller dies. Use the Kindled and Charged condition pills to track who is what.

notes.label: Terrain
notes.text: Back corridors and service passages: lit by glowworm lanterns in jiggly sacks — staff can douse them, and so can the party, which hands Tabby total concealment (Umbral Sight makes her invisible to darkvision in darkness). Guards on post in a public room have passive Perception 10; the same guard on a back-corridor patrol uses its full 15. Rooms hang separately and are joined by open-air walkways and flying buttresses — a fight on a walkway has a long drop into the Overgrowth on both sides.

notes.label: THE RED ANT QUEEN — read before mustering her
notes.text: She is on the sheet so she is there if the party corners her, NOT because this is a fight they can have. CR 13 against three 6th-level PCs: her Multiattack is 96 damage against a party whose entire pool is 118, and Crown of Embers is 55 in a 30 ft. burst — more than any one of them has. Two traits do the real work. Legendary Resistance means Hypnotic Pattern and Hold Person, the party's only genuine answer to something this size, just get declined three times. A Hive Unto Herself regenerates her 20 HP a round while any red ant is within 60 ft. of her, on 348 HP, and Call the Brood refills the room — so they cannot out-damage her without clearing her colony first, which is a longer job than one fight. If she comes out, the correct outcome is the party running. Her vanity is the only lever in the block: she stops to be admired, and would rather be admired than win.

notes.label: Queen — lair and initiative
notes.text: Her lair actions only work in the Throne Room and the Core, and fire on initiative count 20 (losing ties), one per round, never the same one twice running. The tracker sorts on the initiative you type in, so give her lair its own row by mustering nothing for it — just watch for the count-20 slot as you step through turns. Her HP is fixed at 348 rather than rolled; 24d12 on a boss swings 216 to 480 and that is not a variance worth having at the table.

notes.label: Registry cross-ref
notes.text: The three guard types are generic palace forces and are deliberately not tracked in memory/NPC_Registry.yaml. The Red Ant Queen now has a full registry entry — what the party knows about her, her hooks, and a pointer to creatures/red_ant_queen.yaml. Read it before running her; her voice is still marked [MORE DETAIL] because the coronation read-aloud has not been written.

notes.label: The Mantible x2
notes.text: Both Nancy and Drix carry a Mantible — two mandibles off the orchid mantis family in Session 6.5, not a sheet error. Each is a 1d8 finesse short sword that can turn invisible 1x per short rest, and Tabby's mantis-spine dagger does the same. That is three invisible blades in the party, all off the same kill.
